claims.assertion: This is a rider-initiated cancellation of an on-demand (instant) RydeX booking, so the only applicable rule is NS-4: no fee applies if the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, and the $6.61 fee applies only if cancellation came after 3 minutes.
The cancellation was recorded at 17:15:05, i.e. 3 min 05 s after acceptance at 17:12:00 — only 5 seconds past the 3-minute line — and the $6.61 cancellation fee was charged (F2, F5).

The driver never reached the pickup point: GPS shows his closest approach was 2185 m away at the moment of cancellation and he never came within 200 m, and the platform never recorded him arriving at the pickup point.

The driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so the driver-side no-show route to charging a fee under NS-1 (i) is not satisfied and this cancellation cannot be treated as a passenger no-show.

The driver confirmed in chat at 17:13 that he was still about 5 minutes away, and his own statement says he was merely "on my way" — the driver never claims the rider failed to show; the rider waited roughly three minutes for a driver 2.2 km out and then booked another ride.
The $6.61 cancellation fee is the only contested charge (no surge applied, multiplier 1.0×), so the disputed sum is fully computable from the fare record as $6.61 and should be returned to the rider.

The rider's profile (663-day account, 2 no-show disputes in 90 days, both upheld) shows a genuine fee-dispute history rather than abuse of the cancellation button, supporting the requested fee reversal.

weaknesses: NS-4 is a hard time line, not an ETA-fairness line: the system record (F2) shows the rider cancelled at 3 min 05 s after matching, i.e. after the 3-minute mark, so on the literal text of NS-4 the $6.61 fee 'stands' and my case relies on NS-7 relief/discretion rather than an automatic refund.

Ryde publishes no rule giving a free cancellation when the driver is late relative to the ETA (NS-8 is informational only and there is no ETA field in the record), so the driver's own chat message 'About 5 min, traffic' (F8) and the 2.2 km gap (F1) cannot by themselves override NS-4 — they are fairness arguments, not a clause.

The driver's profile is clean (F14: 4.1-year account, 900 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes upheld), so there is no pattern evidence of cancellation-fee abuse and no basis to ask for a flag_account against him under NS-2/NS-3.

points.response: Agreed on the framework: NS-0 routes a rider-cancelled instant booking into NS-4, and my case is built on exactly that clause rather than on NS-1/NS-2.

The 5-second margin is decisive, not trivial: NS-4 draws a bright line at 3 minutes and the system record (F2) places cancellation at 17:15:05, i.e. after the line, so the $6.61 fee is chargeable and no refund is owed on NS-4.

The 2185 m gap and the missing arrival record are irrelevant to a rider cancellation: NS-1/NS-2 apply only to a driver-cancelled trip where the driver claims a no-show, and NS-4 expressly makes the rider's remedy an appeal to Ryde under NS-7, not an automatic refund.

The null "I'm Here" timestamp (F4) defeats nothing here, because no passenger no-show fee was ever assessed — the fee on record is the rider's own cancellation fee (F5), so NS-1 (i) is not an element of this case.

The rider's own chat message at 17:12 asking "How long will you be?" (F7) shows she knew the driver had not yet arrived and still cancelled at 3:05, and the driver answering "About 5 min, traffic" (F8) is consistent with him actively driving toward pickup, which NS-4 does not treat as a ground to waive the fee.
The $6.61 is computable from the fare record (F5) but computability is not entitlement: NS-4 makes it payable once the 3-minute mark is passed, and F2 shows it was, so no amount should be returned.

A profile may support an outcome but never decide the case, and the rider's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F13) is at least as consistent with repeated late cancellations as with legitimate fee disputes; the driver's own record is clean (F14: 1495 days, 900 trips, 0 disputes upheld).

This is a rider-initiated cancellation of an instant RydeX booking, so NS-0 routes the case exclusively through NS-4: with cancelled_by = rider, the fee turns solely on whether the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching [F2][NS-0]. The system timeline is decisive on that point: acceptance at 17:12:00 and rider cancellation at 17:15:05 is 185 s, i.e. 3 min 05 s after matching, so the >3:00 branch of NS-4 is met and the $6.61 cancellation fee is chargeable [F2][F5][NS-4]. Per the procedural rule that system records (gps / timeline / fare) override statements, the rider's chat and the driver's "on my way" statement cannot move the timeline [F8][F9][NS-4].

The driver-side no-show machinery does not apply and does not need to be satisfied: the fee on record is the rider's own cancellation fee, not a passenger no-show fee [F2][F5][NS-0]. Consistently, the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and no arrival was logged, so no NS-1 no-show fee (and no $4.50 driver share) was ever assessed [F3][F4][NS-1]. The 2185 m closest approach and the null arrival record therefore neither create nor defeat the rider's NS-4 fee; they only confirm the cancellation was not a driver-cancelled no-show case [F1][F3][NS-0].

The driver's "traffic" explanation is not needed to justify any reroute or delay, and to the extent it was raised, the traffic record does not support severe congestion: only SIMS AVENUE EAST band 3 (20–29 km/h) with no incidents and fair weather [F10][F11][F12][RD-4]. No RD-type deviation is in issue here, so no exemption analysis is required.

Profiles cannot decide the case: the rider's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days and the driver's clean 90-day record are weighed as context only [F13][F14][NS-4]. Because the rider cancelled 5 seconds past the bright line, the disputed amount is not returnable on any clause, and no clause (RD-6, NS-2) calls for an account action on these facts.

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee (no refund); notify the rider that NS-7 relief for the 5-second overrun is a matter for Ryde's discretion, and log the case as a fee-dispute inquiry only — no account action against either party.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a rider-initiated cancellation of an instant RydeX booking, so NS-0 routes the case exclusively through NS-4: with cancelled_by = rider, the fee turns solely on whether the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching [F2][NS-0]. The system timeline is decisive on that point: acceptance at 17:12:00 and rider cancellation at 17:15:05 is 185 s, i.e. 3 min 05 s after matching, so the >3:00 branch of NS-4 is met and the $6.61 cancellation fee is chargeable [F2][F5][NS-4]. Per the procedural rule that system records (gps / timeline / fare) override statements, the rider's chat and the driver's "on my way" statement cannot move the timeline [F8][F9][NS-4].

The driver-side no-show machinery does not apply and does not need to be satisfied: the fee on record is the rider's own cancellation fee, not a passenger no-show fee [F2][F5][NS-0]. Consistently, the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and no arrival was logged, so no NS-1 no-show fee (and no $4.50 driver share) was ever assessed [F3][F4][NS-1]. The 2185 m closest approach and the null arrival record therefore neither create nor defeat the rider's NS-4 fee; they only confirm the cancellation was not a driver-cancelled no-show case [F1][F3][NS-0].

The driver's "traffic" explanation is not needed to justify any reroute or delay, and to the extent it was raised, the traffic record does not support severe congestion: only SIMS AVENUE EAST band 3 (20–29 km/h) with no incidents and fair weather [F10][F11][F12][RD-4]. No RD-type deviation is in issue here, so no exemption analysis is required.

Profiles cannot decide the case: the rider's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days and the driver's clean 90-day record are weighed as context only [F13][F14][NS-4]. Because the rider cancelled 5 seconds past the bright line, the disputed amount is not returnable on any clause, and no clause (RD-6, NS-2) calls for an account action on these facts.

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: This is a rider-initiated cancellation of an on-demand (instant) RydeX booking, so the only applicable rule is NS-4: no fee applies if the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, and the $6.61 fee applies only if cancellation came after 3 minutes.
The cancellation was recorded at 17:15:05, i.e. 3 min 05 s after acceptance at 17:12:00 — only 5 seconds past the 3-minute line — and the $6.61 cancellation fee was charged (F2, F5).

The driver never reached the pickup point: GPS shows his closest approach was 2185 m away at the moment of cancellation and he never came within 200 m, and the platform never recorded him arriving at the pickup point.

The driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so the driver-side no-show route to charging a fee under NS-1 (i) is not satisfied and this cancellation cannot be treated as a passenger no-show.

The driver confirmed in chat at 17:13 that he was still about 5 minutes away, and his own statement says he was merely "on my way" — the driver never claims the rider failed to show; the rider waited roughly three minutes for a driver 2.2 km out and then booked another ride.
The $6.61 cancellation fee is the only contested charge (no surge applied, multiplier 1.0×), so the disputed sum is fully computable from the fare record as $6.61 and should be returned to the rider.

The rider's profile (663-day account, 2 no-show disputes in 90 days, both upheld) shows a genuine fee-dispute history rather than abuse of the cancellation button, supporting the requested fee reversal.

weaknesses: NS-4 is a hard time line, not an ETA-fairness line: the system record (F2) shows the rider cancelled at 3 min 05 s after matching, i.e. after the 3-minute mark, so on the literal text of NS-4 the $6.61 fee 'stands' and my case relies on NS-7 relief/discretion rather than an automatic refund.

Ryde publishes no rule giving a free cancellation when the driver is late relative to the ETA (NS-8 is informational only and there is no ETA field in the record), so the driver's own chat message 'About 5 min, traffic' (F8) and the 2.2 km gap (F1) cannot by themselves override NS-4 — they are fairness arguments, not a clause.

The driver's profile is clean (F14: 4.1-year account, 900 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes upheld), so there is no pattern evidence of cancellation-fee abuse and no basis to ask for a flag_account against him under NS-2/NS-3.

claims.assertion: This is an instant booking cancelled by the rider 3 min 5 s after acceptance (17:12:00 → 17:15:05), which is more than 3 minutes after matching, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is properly chargeable and the driver's entitlement stands.
The cancellation was made by the rider, not the driver, so the NS-1 / NS-2 no-show analysis does not apply and there is no basis to refund on any driver-cancellation ground.

The rider's complaint that 'the driver was still far away after 3 minutes' is contradicted by her own conduct and the record: she cancelled at 3:05, and the driver was actively en route and told her the ETA was about 5 minutes, so her own delay in waiting was the cause of the cancellation, not any abandonment by the driver.

No exemption applies to this cancellation: no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window, and Ryde publishes no rule allowing a rider to cancel free of charge merely because the driver has not yet arrived.
The driver has a clean 90-day record (900 trips, 0 disputes upheld) while the rider has 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days, weighing against a finding that this fee was improperly collected.

weaknesses: The $6.61 fee on this record is the standard cancellation fee and contains no portion payable to the driver (the $4.50 driver share attaches only to a passenger no-show under NS-1, which is not established here), so the driver gains essentially nothing from the fee being kept and cannot claim compensation for lost time.

The strongest contrary facts are F1 (driver never came within 200 m of the pickup, closest approach 2185 m at 17:15:05) and F3/F4 (driver_arrived_at and driver_pressed_here_at are both null) — the rider will argue these show the driver was never close enough for the trip to be viable and that a 3:05 cancellation was reasonable, and F8 (driver's own 'About 5 min, traffic' estimate) undercuts any claim of imminent arrival.

F10 shows SIMS AVENUE EAST at speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) during 17:07–17:20, which supports the driver's 'traffic' explanation but, being band 3 only, is not severe congestion and cannot justify any reroute or delay excuse under RD-4.

The rider's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F13) can be read as evidence that she repeatedly cancels and then claims refunds, but a profile fact may not decide the case, so it cannot by itself defeat her claim.

points.response: Conceded on the timing arithmetic: F2 does show cancellation at 3 min 05 s after acceptance, so the literal NS-4 threshold is crossed and I do not dispute that the record shows the fee as chargeable on its face; my request rests on NS-7 relief and on the fact that no NS-1 no-show ground exists at all (F3, F4).

This cuts against the driver, not for him: NS-0 routes a rider-cancellation instant booking only through NS-4, and NS-1's driver-side conditions (ii) and (iii) are nowhere near satisfied because GPS puts the driver 2185 m away and never within 200 m (F1) and driver_pressed_here_at is null (F4), so no passenger no-show — and no $4.50 driver share — is established.

'Actively en route' is not in the record: GPS shows the closest approach was 2185 m at 17:15:05 and the platform never logged arrival (F1, F3), while the driver's own 17:13 message promised 'about 5 min' (F8) — so at 3 min 05 s the trip was still not viable and the rider's ~3-minute wait followed exactly what the driver stated.

I do not rely on any traffic exemption: F11 records no incident and F10 shows only speed band 3 (20–29 km/h), which cannot excuse a delay under RD-4, and F12 shows fair weather — so the driver's 'traffic' explanation is unsupported and the reason for the fee is the fee itself, not a justified delay.

Profile facts cannot decide the case under NS-4/NS-7, and my client's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F13) show she reports genuine fee problems rather than abuse, while the driver's clean record (F14) is irrelevant because he never reached the pickup point (F1, F3).
Agreed on the framework: NS-0 routes a rider-cancelled instant booking into NS-4, and my case is built on exactly that clause rather than on NS-1/NS-2.

The 5-second margin is decisive, not trivial: NS-4 draws a bright line at 3 minutes and the system record (F2) places cancellation at 17:15:05, i.e. after the line, so the $6.61 fee is chargeable and no refund is owed on NS-4.

The 2185 m gap and the missing arrival record are irrelevant to a rider cancellation: NS-1/NS-2 apply only to a driver-cancelled trip where the driver claims a no-show, and NS-4 expressly makes the rider's remedy an appeal to Ryde under NS-7, not an automatic refund.

The null "I'm Here" timestamp (F4) defeats nothing here, because no passenger no-show fee was ever assessed — the fee on record is the rider's own cancellation fee (F5), so NS-1 (i) is not an element of this case.

The rider's own chat message at 17:12 asking "How long will you be?" (F7) shows she knew the driver had not yet arrived and still cancelled at 3:05, and the driver answering "About 5 min, traffic" (F8) is consistent with him actively driving toward pickup, which NS-4 does not treat as a ground to waive the fee.
The $6.61 is computable from the fare record (F5) but computability is not entitlement: NS-4 makes it payable once the 3-minute mark is passed, and F2 shows it was, so no amount should be returned.

A profile may support an outcome but never decide the case, and the rider's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F13) is at least as consistent with repeated late cancellations as with legitimate fee disputes; the driver's own record is clean (F14: 1495 days, 900 trips, 0 disputes upheld).
